headline: Former US Vice President Kamala Harris has warned in Seoul that the chance to put safety limits on AI is closing and has urged the United States to work with China on AI rules.
score_reason: Pool score kept: an on-record speech reported by Reuters, but by a person who holds no office and announces no policy.
importance_line: A former vice president who may run again urging AI limits and cooperation with China matters to the public mainly as a signal of Democratic positions before the midterm elections, then to lawmakers and AI firms, but she holds no office and proposes no specific rule.
summary: Reuters reports that Kamala Harris, the former US vice president, told an audience at the Asan Institute for Policy Studies in Seoul on Wednesday 14 Oct that "the window is shutting" for AI safeguards and that governments and companies must act now against three existential dangers she named: cybersecurity threats, AI-enabled weapons and AI systems that escape human control. She also urged the United States to engage China on international AI rules, saying "there is room for cooperation where our interests are aligned", and Reuters notes that she is campaigning for Democrats before the midterm elections and has not decided whether to run for president in 2028.
notes: Reuters original blocked (401); text read on Internazionale's Reuters wire copy (https://www.internazionale.it/ultime-notizie-reuters/2026/10/14/kamala-harris-warns-window-closing-for-ai-safeguards-urges-us-china-cooperation). Url kept as the Reuters original.
